correctness.rationale: From A²=(d−mu)I+(lambda−mu)A+mu J the two nonconstant adjacency eigenvalues r≥0 and s<0 are the roots of x²−(lambda−mu)x−(d−mu); the centered two-round Euclidean norm is max(|(1−(d−r)p)(1−(d−r)q)|,|(1−(d−s)p)(1−(d−s)q)|). If lambda≥mu the first product is positive and strictly decreases in both gains; it is sharp at p=q=1/d and dominates the negative-mode product. If lambda<mu,r>0, a positive convex combination of the two products is a bilinear function F(p,q)=R_*+(1−R_*)(1−dp)(1−dq)≥R_*; equality and balancing force unordered {p,q}={1/d,1/(d+mu−lambda)}. At r=0, mu=d and the two spectral roots force the same pair with R_*=0. Direct multiplication and A² relation yield P(q)P(p)=R_*I+(1−R_*)J/N and exclude nonidentity mean-field products lambda>mu. This is an all-parameter analytic certificate; independent Petersen check d=3,lambda=0,mu=1 gives gains 1/3,1/4, both nontrivial products 1/6, and 10x10 kernel I/6+J/12. The eight-graph exact-rational checker was inspected, not treated as proof.
